body_markdown:
The month of October is a wild ride. Residents are decorating balconies, package rooms are overflowing, and the first cold snap sends work orders flying. Somewhere in the middle of it all, your on-site team is holding everything together. So, here's a seasonal question worth asking:


*when it comes to keeping your people happy, are you handing out tricks or treats?*


Some perks look sweet from the outside but leave teams feeling empty. Others cost very little and make a real difference. Let's sort the candy bowl.


##


**How to "Treat" Your Property Team**


**Trick: The pizza party that replaces a real fix.**


Pizza is great. Pizza as a substitute for solving a staffing gap? Not so much. When a leasing office is down a person and the maintenance team is covering two properties, a lunch in the clubhouse feels more like a consolation prize than a thank you.


**Treat: Coverage when they need it most.**


Nothing says "we've got your back" like a fully staffed team. Bringing in


[temporary property management staff](https://propmgtdiv.bgsf.com/) during peak seasons, vacations, or turnover gives your core team room to breathe. And breathing room is the fastest cure for burnout.


**Trick: "We're like a family here."**


Family is wonderful. But teams don't want to hear it when they're working weekends without backup or skipping lunch to cover the front desk. Big words without follow-through land with a thud.


**Treat: Clear expectations and realistic workloads.**


Property teams want to know what success looks like and have the tools to get there. Defined roles, reasonable unit counts per tech, and a schedule they can actually plan around will do more for on-site team retention than any slogan.


**Trick: Recognition once a year.**


The annual award ceremony is nice. The other 364 days matter more. If the only time your maintenance tech hears "great job" is at the holiday party, that's a missed opportunity.


**Treat: Real-time, specific appreciation.**


A quick shout-out after a tough move-in weekend or a handwritten note when a resident leaves a glowing review can have a much larger impact than you imagine. Employee appreciation for property teams works best when it's frequent, personal, and tied to something real. It doesn't have to be fancy. It has to be sincere.


**Trick: Training that's just a binder.**


Handing a new hire a stack of SOPs and wishing them luck is a classic trick. They'll get there eventually, but they'll be stressed the whole way.


**Treat: Growth they can see.**


Leasing pros want to sharpen their sales skills. Maintenance techs want certifications like HVAC or CPO. Assistant managers want a path to the top job. Invest in their growth, and they'll invest in your property.


**Trick: Ignoring the hiring crunch until it's a crisis**


Waiting until three positions are open before you start recruiting is the scariest move of the season. By then, your remaining team is exhausted, and residents are noticing.


**Treat: A staffing partner who's already on it.**


Smart operators plan ahead, especially heading into year-end. Having a trusted partner for maintenance technician staffing, leasing support, and on-site management means you can fill gaps fast with people who know the industry. No scrambling. No guesswork.


##


**The Sweetest Treat of All**


Here's the truth: Your property team doesn't need a bigger candy bowl; they need support, respect, and enough hands on deck to do great work without burning out. Give them that, and you'll see it everywhere. Happier residents, smoother operations, and teams that stick around for the long haul.
